reviews.comment: She is a very kind and approachable professor who genuinely wants her students to do well. Her exams can be challenging, so I would recommend studying several days in advance rather than waiting until the last minute. Attendance is also important because she takes attendance and uses iClicker quizzes during class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a difficult class but has been one of my overall favorites at TAMU. You will only succeed if you go to the class, take notes, and actively engage with the lectures/class material. Dr. Krasteva is a great professor and I highly recommend this class if you're willing to put the effort in, I found it super interesting!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Krasteva. She's very sweet and wants to help you, you just have to ask. Her content is tricky, but she isn't trying to make the class hard. You can tell she really wants to see her students succeed.

Easily my favorite professor in the econ department. Not the easiest courses ever, but the courseload was manageable- the lectures were always engaging, and by actually doing the assignments, you should be well prepared for all the tests.

Prof Krasteva is clearly very passionate about the material she is teaching which makes the lectures much more interesting. The tests were difficult ish but if you go to class and review the unit models beforehand you'll be fine. I would take this class again if I could.

I adore Dr. Krasteva; she cares about her students. Lectures were rly interesting but her exams were hard Don't know how I got A's on them when I guessed on more than half of the exam. She does a great job explaining different subject laws, but her exams were the hardest I've ever taken. Take her if you're willing to put in a lot of time and work.

If you do not like to read and find court cases boring, avoid this class. Otherwise, you should definitely sign up. Prof. Kravesta is fantastic, and really cares about the material. If you show her you are making an effort, by asking her questions after class, or going to office hours, she will help you out. Difficult tests, but the curve helps.

A lot of outside reading for this course. I felt that the math parts were difficult and not explained very well but she's very nice and caring and easily accessible outside of class during office hours

Tough class, but one of the most enjoyable/educational ECON classes I have taken at A&M. A great class if you want to dip your toe into law and learn some terminology. The professor can come off as a bit mean/intimidating, but she is actually caring. You will need to do the reading and have good reading comprehension to do well in this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Prof Krasteva is very kind and helpful with any questions you might have. The exams and readings are pretty difficult though and you will probably spend a while trying to understand them. You need to go to class for participation, & studying the homework for the exams is crucial.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The tests are way harder than they need to be. You can have all the information down and still struggle on the test. Many of the questions are from readings and are unclear even if you understand the reading entirely.

Dr. Krasteva has been one of the best professors I've had at TAMU. This class can be challenging and is definitely not for everyone. The readings are LONG and difficult to read but the class is really interesting and she cares about her students. Grades are fair.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance and in class quizzes count for your grade. Curves tests by how many points it takes to get the highest grade to a 100 (i.e. highest grade in the class was a 88, there will be a 12 point curve added to everybody's tests)
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy
